brief.idea: a girl and her llama must cross the mountain pass to bring medicine before the snow
brief.setting: a village high in the Andes of Peru

premise.title: Nina and the Snow Pass
premise.logline: Nina must cross the mountain pass to fetch medicine from the snow cave before the first snowfall, or her mother will not survive the fever.
premise.theme: Love gives even the smallest the strength to face the tallest mountain.
premise.hook: A healer bursts into the house: 'The snow is coming early, and the fever will take her unless we get the herb from the snow cave!'
premise.stakes: Mama Rosa's life depends on the medicine, and if the snow blocks the pass, no one can get through until spring.
tools: ticking clock: before the snow closes the pass
rising stakes: the weather worsens and the trail crumbles
false victory: they reach the cave but the snow starts
the 'it cannot get worse, and it gets worse' beat: the rope bridge sways as the wind picks up
premise.want: to bring the medicine back to the village
premise.obstacle: the mountain pass and the coming snow
premise.clock: before the first snow blocks the pass, by nightfall
premise.normalDay: Nina helps her mother tend the llamas and dreams of the world beyond the mountains.
premise.whyToday: The healer says a fever has struck Mama Rosa, and the only cure is in the snow cave, but the first snow is expected today.
premise.whyCare: Nina gently comforts Canela when she is scared of the wind, showing her kindness.
spine: Once upon a time, there was a girl named Nina who lived in a high Andean village with her mother, Mama Rosa, and her loyal llama, Canela.
Every day, Nina helped her mother tend the llamas and fetch water from the well, always gazing at the forbidden mountain pass.
Until one day, Mama Rosa fell ill with a fever, and the healer said the only cure was a rare herb in the snow cave at the top of the pass, but the first snow was coming.
Because of that, Nina and Canela set off up the steep trail, crossing a rope bridge and climbing a narrow ledge, with the wind howling and snow beginning to fall.
Until finally, they reached the snow cave, found the herb, and raced back down as the pass filled with snow, just making it home.
Ever since then, Nina was known as the bravest girl in the village, and she and Canela always helped those in need.

setup.what: Nina says, 'I'll bring the snow-herb back before the snow, Mamita.'
Mama Rosa says, 'The pass is closing, palomita. The wind already bites.'
Mama Rosa says, 'If the fever does not break by nightfall, I will not see the morning.'
The snow clouds darken over the pass and the well water shivers with the first cold gust.
Mama Rosa says, 'She has mountain feet. Let her choose the stones,' as Canela walks the narrow stone wall without slipping.
